title: Attorney Network Standards — Demand Letters, Address Verification, Servicemember Affidavits and Service Attempts (Legal Forwarding Agreements)
content:
Issued to the collection attorneys of Ridgeline's network who handle matters under the Legal Forwarding Agreements. For each forwarding programme, this standard fixes the number of attorney demand letters, the calendar days after the last letter before a suit may be filed, whether the debtor's address is verified by skip trace before filing, whether a servicemember status affidavit is filed before a default judgment is sought, and how many service-of-process attempts are covered before extra service costs are incurred.

## Standard by programme

| Programme | Attorney demand letters | Days after the last letter before a suit may be filed | Skip trace before filing | Servicemember status affidavit before default judgment | Service attempts included |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Attorney Demand Program | 1 | 30 | No | No | 0 |
| Small Claims Suit Program | 1 | 14 | Yes | Yes | 2 |
| Client-Advanced Cost Suit Program | 1 | 30 | Yes | Yes | 3 |
| Agency-Advanced Cost Suit Program | 1 | 30 | Yes | Yes | 3 |
| Judgment Enforcement Program | 0 | 0 | No | Yes | 0 |
| Full-Service Litigation Program | 2 | 30 | Yes | Yes | 3 |

## Terms explained

1. **Attorney demand letters.** The number of attorney demand letters sent before suit, or, where the programme files no suit, as the whole service. Under the Attorney Demand Program the single letter is the whole service; the Judgment Enforcement Program sends none; the Full-Service Litigation Program sends two.
2. **Waiting days after the last letter.** The calendar days after the last attorney demand letter before a suit may be filed: 14 under the Small Claims Suit Program and 30 under the Client-Advanced Cost, Agency-Advanced Cost and Full-Service Litigation programmes.
3. **Skip trace.** Whether the debtor's address is verified by skip trace before filing. Yes for the four programmes that file suits; No for the Attorney Demand Program and the Judgment Enforcement Program.
4. **Servicemember status affidavit.** Whether a servicemember status affidavit is filed before a default judgment is sought. Every programme shows Yes except the Attorney Demand Program.
5. **Service attempts included.** The number of service-of-process attempts covered before extra service costs are incurred: 2 under the Small Claims Suit Program, 3 under the Client-Advanced Cost, Agency-Advanced Cost and Full-Service Litigation programmes, and 0 under the Attorney Demand Program and the Judgment Enforcement Program.

## Illustration on hypothetical dates

Under the Full-Service Litigation Program two letters are sent. If, hypothetically, the second and last letter went out on 1 April, the 30-day waiting period is counted from that second letter, not from the first.

Under the Small Claims Suit Program, a hypothetical matter whose service of process takes a third attempt has gone beyond the 2 attempts covered, so extra service costs are incurred for that third attempt.
